evidenceAudit.scope: Children and adolescents under 18: the Saudi national immunization schedule, checking status at every contact, true contraindications, and planning catch-up for missed or unknown doses. Verified against the Saudi PHA Clinical Preventive Guideline 2023 (Table 1, national schedule), the UK Green Book Chapter 6 (contraindications) and UKHSA guidance on uncertain or incomplete immunisation status. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.

pathophysiology.summary: Vaccines prime adaptive immunity (antibodies and memory cells) so a later exposure is controlled before disease develops. High coverage also protects those who cannot be vaccinated. PHA recommends routine vaccination against 17 vaccine-preventable diseases.
keyMechanisms: Inactivated and subunit vaccines need a primary series and boosters.
Live attenuated vaccines (MMR, varicella, rotavirus, OPV, BCG) give long-lasting immunity but can harm the immunosuppressed.
Maternal antibody interferes with measles vaccine early in infancy — hence timing from 9–12 months.

symptoms: Check the vaccination record (Mother Health Passport / child record) at every visit.
Ask about previous reactions, immunosuppression and current illness.
redFlags: Fever above 38.5 °C — postpone until recovered (Green Book Ch. 6)
Child of a mother on immunosuppressive biologics in pregnancy — delay live vaccines (Green Book Ch. 6)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Not a reason to delay (Green Book Ch. 6).
Not a contraindication to MMR (Green Book Ch. 6).

clinicalManagement.title: Saudi national schedule (PHA Table 1)
actions: 2 and 4 months: HepB, rotavirus, DTaP, Hib, PCV, IPV.
6 months: HepB, rotavirus, DTaP, Hib, PCV, IPV, OPV, BCG.
9 months: measles, MCV4. 12 months: PCV, OPV, MCV4, MMR.
18 months: DTaP, Hib, OPV, HepA, varicella, MMR. 24 months: HepA.
4–6 years: DTaP, OPV, varicella, MMR. 11 years: Tdap; HPV (females). 12 years: HPV (females). 18 years: MCV4.
Influenza from 6 months of age (PHA Table 1).

clinicalManagement.title: Catch-up principles (UKHSA)
actions: No reliable history: assume unimmunised and plan a full course.
Course started but not completed: resume — do not restart or repeat doses.
Use the fewest visits and shortest timescale; usual minimum gap 4 weeks between visits.
Measles-, MMR- or varicella-containing doses given before 12 months do not count; 2 MMR doses at least 4 weeks apart.
Transfer children arriving part-way through another schedule onto the national schedule for age.

clinicalManagement.title: Contraindications (Green Book Ch. 6)
actions: Avoid a vaccine after confirmed anaphylaxis to a previous dose or component.
No live vaccines during high-dose steroids (over 2 mg/kg/day in children under 20 kg for more than 1 week) or within 3 months of stopping, and within 6 months of chemotherapy.
Postpone if febrile above 38.5 °C; minor illness is not a reason to delay.

adjustments: Dose volume and route per the SFDA-registered product leaflet — not reproduced here
monitoring: Observe for immediate reactions; anaphylaxis treatment available (Green Book Ch. 6)
contraindications: Confirmed anaphylaxis to a previous dose or to a vaccine component (Green Book Ch. 6)
Live vaccines (MMR, varicella): avoid in significant immunodeficiency or immunosuppressive therapy, and in pregnancy (Green Book Ch. 6)
Postpone if acutely unwell with fever above 38.5 °C; minor illness is not a reason to delay (Green Book Ch. 6)
